title: Chicken drumstick, baked, coated, skin / coating not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken drumsticks are the lower leg portion of the bird, containing meat, bone and sometimes skin. When baked with a coating they develop a crispy crust, while the skin/coating is usually not eaten.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks are used in many world cuisines, from American BBQ to Asian curries.
Baking in the oven retains more nutrients than deep‑frying.
Coatings can be made from whole‑grain flour, breadcrumbs or nut meals, adding extra fiber.
Chicken skin is higher in fat, so it is often removed to lower the calorie count.
Poultry meat is a highly digestible source of protein suitable for most diets.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Drumsticks provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B6, niacin and riboflavin support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health, blood formation and wound healing.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Makes them suitable for low‑carb and keto diets.

items.title: Provides collagen
items.content: Bone and connective tissue contribute a modest amount of collagen, beneficial for skin and joints.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Fat in the skin
items.content: If the skin is left on, the dish can become higher in calories and saturated fat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked meat may contain Salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C.

items.title: Sodium in the coating
items.content: Pre‑made breading mixes often contain salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you watch sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the drumsticks hot, pulling the meat off the bone. The skin/coating can stay in the dish for flavor but is not eaten. Pair them with vegetable sides, rice, potatoes, or slice cooled meat into salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fresh drumsticks keep in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Cooked pieces can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat to 75 °C before serving.
